draft.title: Human-induced environmental change
card: Human-induced change is change to an environment that is caused by people, not by natural processes such as a lightning fire or a volcanic eruption.
Common causes are land clearing, pollution, overusing water, building, and burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas.
Sustainability means using an environment in a way that still meets needs in the future. These changes can reduce the sustainability of a place.
For example, taking more water from a river than rain refills can dry out wetlands. Farms and towns that rely on the river may then struggle too.
draft.remember: Human-induced change comes from people's actions. It can reduce a place's sustainability.

a.q: Which of these is an example of human-induced environmental change?
opts: Draining a wetland to build a housing estate
A river flooding after an unusually wet season
A volcano covering a valley with ash
Lightning starting a fire in a forest
a.why: People chose to drain the wetland, so the change is human-induced. The other three are natural events that happen without human action.
a.clue: Which change happens because of a human decision?

b.q: Farmers near a river in Victoria take far more water than the rain refills, and the river begins to dry out. Why does this reduce the sustainability of the area?
opts: The water may not be there to meet needs in the future
The farmers have changed the area in a natural way
The river will always flow again after the next flood
The change only affects the river and not the farms
b.why: Sustainability means still meeting needs in the future. If more water is taken than is refilled, less is left for later, so the place is less sustainable. Floods may help sometimes, but the card does not say a river will always recover.
b.clue: Think about what is left for people in the future.

a.best: Draining a wetland to build a housing estate

b.best: The water may not be there to meet needs in the future

problems.detail: The right option stands out. It is the only one with a hedge ('may'), while two distractors use absolutes ('always', 'only') that students learn to rule out. It is also the only option that mentions 'needs in the future', which echoes the card's definition of sustainability and the clue's 'in the future'. A student could pick it without understanding the idea.
